newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: BOXING-HOLYFIELD DUCKS COMMENT ON TYSON BAN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-HOLYFIELD DUCKS COMMENT ON TYSON BAN.

text.p: World heavyweight champion Evander Holyfield, on holiday in South Africa, ducked comment on Wednesday on rival Mike Tyson's boxing ban and $3 million fine for biting a chunk off his ear.
"Mr. Holyfield is on the phone to his lawyer, Mr. Jim Thomas, and then he's going out for dinner," an aide told reporters waiting for the champion.
Holyfield arrived in Cape Town on a private flight from East London, where his promotional coaching tour ended on Wednesday.
"No comment", he told reporters as he left East London.

In Cape Town, airport officials closed the apron to reporters as he arrived and at the city's oldest five-star hotel staff liaised with bodyguards to ensure that a waiting television crew caught no more than a distant glimpse of the boxer.
After an hour-long game of cat and mouse with reporters, Holyfield was bundled into a minibus and driven off for a late dinner in the city.

The aide said Holyfield had nothing to add to his statement when he arrived in South Africa on Sunday and said that as a Christian he had forgiven Tyson for biting his ears during their June 28 championship bout.
Tyson was disqualified in the third round after twice biting Holyfield and taking a portion off the top of his right ear.

The five-member Nevada State Athletic Commission voted unanimously on Wednesday to impose the maximum punishment and revoke Tyson's license to box in the state, effectively banning him from boxing in the United States.
The 31-year-old boxer, who once dominated the sport, can apply for reinstatement in one year but if his application is denied he must wait another year to try again.
The revocation could constitute a lifetime ban.
